text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

Thanks for reaching out about your father's house. I'm the facilitator for this. I'll keep one running list of concerns, numbered in the order they come up, and share it whenever it changes. I don't make legal decisions or move money, but I can help you three find a plan you can all live with.

Here is the list so far:

1. C says A wants to buy the house with her husband at a family discount, and C will not agree to that.
2. C says B could use some money from the house.

I've asked A and B for their own concerns so everyone's view is on the list. Can you tell me what outcome you would be comfortable with, and what your main worry is?

I’d be comfortable with a plan that gives each of us a fair financial share. If A buys the house, I won’t subsidize a family discount. My main worry is being pressured to give up my share—and damaging things with my twin over it.

I suggest this path, and I'd like your view on it. First, one of you finds out who holds the will, likely a lawyer or the person who handled your father's papers, so all three read the same document. Second, you get an independent valuation of the house, so you are negotiating from one shared figure. Third, any discount below that valuation is money coming out of B's and C's shares, not just yours, so it has to be agreed by them, and it may be simpler for the discount to come out of your own share only. Fourth, if A and her husband buy the house, A pays B and C for their shares, which would give B her studio money.

Do you agree to the first two steps, finding the will and getting a valuation? I can't do either myself.
Yes. I agree we should find the will and get an independent valuation, and make sure all three of us see the same information.
